name: sticky-sections
summary: Full-height panels that pin in turn: as the next one scrolls over it, a panel dims to brightness(60%) contrast(135%) and drifts up 15%, while the image inside it slides 40% and tips -20deg.

brightness.description: Percent brightness a panel dims to as the next one covers it. Upstream's brightness(60%).

contrast.description: Percent contrast a panel is pushed to as it dims. Upstream's contrast(135%).

lift.description: Percent of its own height a panel drifts up by. Upstream's yPercent: -15.

imageLift.description: Percent of its own height the image inside a panel drifts up by. Upstream's yPercent: -40.

imageRotate.description: Degrees the image tips over by. Upstream's rotation: -20.

deviations.what: The gsap.timeline with scrollTrigger { start: 'top top', end: '+=100%', scrub: true } becomes an anime createTimeline with autoplay: onScroll({ enter: 'top top', leave: 'top bottom', sync: true }), and ease 'none' becomes 'linear' while 'power1.in' becomes 'inQuad'.
deviations.why: GSAP is banned here: its licence forbids use in tools that let people build animations without code. The mapping is exact rather than approximate. A panel is one viewport tall, so its bottom reaching the container's top is one viewport of scroll after its top did, which is what '+=100%' means; anime's sync of 1 applies no smoothing lerp, which is what scrub: true means; and GSAP's power scale is power1=Quad, so power1.in is inQuad. anime's threshold strings read '<container edge> <target edge>', the reverse of how they scan, so the leave is written 'top bottom' -- with the tokens the other way round offsetEnd lands before offsetStart, the distance clamps to zero and the panel silently never moves.

deviations.what: A scrubbed timeline is given a nominal SCRUB_DURATION of 100 that both tweens share.
deviations.why: GSAP's scrub maps the scroll range onto the timeline without the timeline needing a length of its own, and there is no upstream number to carry over. anime seeks a timeline by progress, so the two tweens only have to be the same length and start together; the value itself is never played.

deviations.what: Lenis and its raf loop are dropped, along with the ScrollTrigger.update call driven off its scroll event and the imagesloaded preload.
deviations.why: Smooth scrolling is a page-level decision and paw-fx ships it as its own effect (smooth-scroll); a section that hijacks the page's scrolling because it happens to be on the page is a bad neighbour, and two sections doing it would fight. anime's onScroll reads native scroll directly. The preload exists to hide a flash of unloaded images and there are no bundled images here to load.

deviations.what: The last panel gets no tween at all, where upstream tweens it to filter 'none' and yPercent 0.
deviations.why: Same outcome, minus an interpolation anime cannot perform. Upstream writes both values as ternaries inside a shared call, and for the last panel they resolve to filter 'none' and yPercent 0: 'none' is not a filter list, so there is nothing between brightness(100%) contrast(100%) and it to interpolate. GSAP quietly sets a value it cannot tween; anime would try to decompose the keyword. Not tweening the last panel says exactly what upstream means.

deviations.what: Only demo 1 is ported. The other fourteen exit treatments, their per-demo palettes and the .content--card / .content--half / .content--perspective layouts are dropped, and .content--sticky's width goes from 100vw to 100%.
deviations.why: Fifteen variants of one structural pattern would be fifteen near-duplicate effects in a registry a site agent queries by name. Demo 1 is the one the repo opens on and the one the article leads with; the rest are worth their own ports if they are ever wanted. 100vw is wider than the section whenever a scrollbar is showing, which pushes the whole page sideways.

deviations.what: The twelve bundled PNGs become a .fx-sticky__img div painting a gradient, and the typekit stylesheet (area-variable) and its font-variation-settings are dropped for a system sans stack.
deviations.why: Codrops' demo artwork is licensed separately from the code and is not ours to redistribute; the image is a slot the panel animates whatever it is given, so a gradient keeps the treatment legible and a site author overrides background-image. The variable font is a hosted stylesheet a generated site cannot fetch offline, and its axis settings do nothing without it.
